item.title: Xi chairs groundbreaking China-Russia-U.S. summit with Putin, Trump
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday chaired a historic summit here with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump, marking the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state. At the summit, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the three leaders had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, outlining their common understandings on issues including the UN reform, energy security, the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and nuclear risk reduction. Xi described the trilateral meeting as being of groundbreaking significance. He said peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos. Peace has been the enduring pursuit of humanity, Xi said, noting that the planet has experienced more than 10,000 wars and that more than 60 conflicts are still underway in various parts of the world. More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the United States, the key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world, he said. RIGHT WAY FOR MAJOR COUNTRIES TO GET ALONG "Humanity, living in the same global village, is a community with a shared future where we all stand to benefit or lose together," Xi said. "In this global village, major countries shoulder special responsibilities. Their positive interaction is not optional, but a must." In recent years, China has been promoting the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era and actively developing the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, with a view to fostering major-country dynamics featuring peaceful coexistence, overall stability and balanced development to the benefit of each other and the world at large, he said. Noting that transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, Xi said the world is not peaceful and testing times reveal responsibilities on one's shoulders. As major countries and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi said. Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. He said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. "On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another," Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. "The Thucydides Trap is by no means a destiny." As the main victors of World War II, the three countries should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes of victory in World War II, Xi said. According to the trilateral declaration, the three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. "Nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons," Xi said. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, and combine their respective strengths in resources, manufacturing and consumption to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. "Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go," Xi said, adding that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. "China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means," he said. POSITIVE, CONSTRUCTIVE AND FRUITFUL SUMMIT Putin said that the victory in World War II brought the three countries together. Safeguarding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and upholding international peace are their shared responsibilities, while properly addressing hotspot issues serves their common interests, he added. Russia stands ready to work with China and the United States to promote free and open international trade, safeguard energy and food security, and strengthen international cooperation on artificial intelligence governance, Putin said. Trump said that the United States, China and Russia, as nuclear powers, bear a special and important responsibility for maintaining world peace and stability. Trump said the summit is a historic event of great importance, drawing global attention. He said the three countries should jointly prevent nuclear proliferation and avert the catastrophic consequences that nuclear weapons could bring to humanity. Noting that dialogue is essential to maintaining stability and achieving peace, Trump said all issues should be resolved through dialogue. He expressed hope that the three countries better protect the planet and make the future safer. The three heads of state also exchanged views on major international and regional issues, including the Ukraine crisis, nuclear non-proliferation, the situations in the Middle East and on the Korean Peninsula. Summarizing main consensus reached at the summit, Xi described the meeting as positive, constructive and fruitful, saying that the three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace. Xi said that the three countries remember their history of fighting side by side during World War II and stressed the need to cherish the hard-won peace. Major countries should take seriously the legitimate security concerns of all nations, he added. Dialogue and negotiation represent the right way to resolve differences, Xi said. "There is hope for peace as long as dialogue does not cease and the door does not close." He stressed that cooperation is the only way to meet challenges, calling for stronger cooperation on the basis of common interests to advance peace and pursue win-win outcomes. "The seeds sown at today's summit will surely take root, sprout, blossom and bear fruit," Xi said, calling on the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, strengthen communication, build common ground through dialogue, promote peace via cooperation, and work together to build a better world. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. item.title: APEC Shenzhen meeting new peak in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation: Chinese FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Thursday that the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting marked a new peak in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation. It was the most important diplomatic event China hosted this year, said Wang, who is also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, at a press conference held after the meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The meeting produced the ambitious, practical and comprehensive APEC Leaders' Shenzhen Outlook, which is the most significant outcome of the APEC "China Year" and a new milestone in APEC cooperation, Wang said. At the meeting, Chinese President Xi Jinping called for building an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. Xi elaborated on China's proposals regarding what kind of Asia-Pacific community should be built and how to build it, Wang noted. Wang said the meeting also injected new momentum into advancing the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. Wang highlighted the upgraded APEC Connectivity Blueprint endorsed at the meeting, which is aimed at advancing infrastructure development, strengthening supply chain connectivity, enhancing policy and regulatory cooperation, and facilitating the movement of people. Wang hailed China's contribution to the endorsement of an APEC statement on harnessing digital and emerging technologies for jobs and prosperity. The statement helps align cooperation on AI and other new technologies to advance high-quality full employment, public services and digital infrastructure, Wang said. The Chinese foreign minister also noted a series of measures Xi announced to boost Asia-Pacific cooperation, including setting up an Asia-Pacific community studies center, a proposal to establish a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation, and financial support for practical cooperation. Wang said the Shenzhen meeting has mapped out the key pillars and priorities for building an Asia-Pacific community and charted a roadmap for implementation. It is fair to say that the journey toward an Asia-Pacific community has truly begun in Shenzhen, Wang said. ■

item.title: China-Russia-U.S. summit a landmark to go down in history: Chinese FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- The China-Russia-U.S. summit was the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of the three countries and is of great significance with a far-reaching impact, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Thursday, calling it a landmark event that will go down in history. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when meeting the press after the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump reached important consensus. The China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace issued after the meeting is instrumental to addressing global challenges and maintaining world peace and stability, Wang said. "You could certainly call it a peace summit." Noting that the top leaders of the three countries exchanged views on the international situation and global challenges, Wang said the summit sent a positive message to the world. Calling the meeting a historic one, Wang said it created a paradigm for interaction between major countries in the new era, and represented a new step in building a new type of major-country relations. It was indeed a major pioneering move in the history of international relations, he added. It was also a landmark meeting showing a sense of responsibility of major countries, Wang noted. Articulating their respective strategic intentions face-to-face, the three leaders agreed to prevent conflict and confrontation and build a paradigm of major-country relations featuring peaceful coexistence, overall stability and balanced development. "This is not only good for the three countries, but also benefits the whole world," Wang said. ■

item.title: "Where there is trade, there is mutual benefit" -- perspectives from APEC CEO Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- "Where there is trade, there is mutual benefit." For renowned U.S. economist Jeffrey Sachs, the idea is simple and clearcut: the global economy need not be a zero-sum game. After attending the 2026 APEC CEO Summit, he made the point with evident enthusiasm: "It's not that we have to choose who wins and who loses. Everybody can win through peaceful cooperation." With the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," this year's APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, a southern Chinese metropolis, brought together more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. In interviews with Xinhua on site, several attendees shared their perspectives on free trade, innovation and cooperation, offering insights into how business leaders view the region's evolving economic landscape and the opportunities it presents. INNOVATION COOPERATION Sachs recounted his journey from Italy to China riding BYD electric vehicles, covering 15,000 km along a route inspired by Marco Polo's journey 750 years ago. "He went by horse, I went by 800 horsepower. This is the breakthrough," he said. Amid rapid technological advances, the economist noted, the prevailing sentiment is one of cooperation, with participants eager to expand trade, attract investment, pursue joint ventures and become part of the Asia-Pacific's growing economic dynamism. This view is echoed by Jacob Cooke, CEO of WPIC, a Canadian e-commerce and technology consultancy that helps global brands grow their businesses in China, Japan, South Korea and Southeast Asia. A frequent traveler to China, Cooke has witnessed firsthand the remarkable pace of innovation in cities such as Shenzhen, Shanghai, Nanjing and Hangzhou. "It's incredible," he said. He pointed to China's approach to artificial intelligence (AI), particularly its open-source and open-weight models and affordable AI solutions, which are increasingly accessible to businesses around the world. At a time when countries across the globe are looking to harness AI for their own development, he said, Chinese companies have focused on making the technology widely available rather than maximizing profits or putting up barriers to access. Seeing Chinese companies embrace this spirit of openness and sharing, much like the people of China, gives him "real optimism," he added. Rosario Navarro, president of Chile's non-profit business federation Sofofa, said Chilean companies were keen to forge partnerships with Chinese enterprises in high-tech fields, including AI. "If we engage Chinese companies with the technology that allows us to be more productive, we can clearly take a leap, and that's what we're waiting for," Navarro added. OPPORTUNITIES IN CHINESE MARKET For many participants, opportunities for cooperation extend beyond technology to include talent development, industrial upgrading and other sectors. Anindya Novyan Bakrie, chairman of the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, identified two closely related competitive advantages of the Chinese market: technology and talent. Beyond trade and business cooperation, he said, Indonesia hopes to explore ways to develop its talent pool through closer collaboration between universities and businesses in the two countries. Technology cooperation, he added, should extend beyond digital technologies and AI to include processing technologies across a wide range of industries, from critical minerals and agricultural products to traditional energy. Agricultural trade is another area where participants see scope for deeper engagement. Carlos Salinas, executive director of East Asia at the U.S. Soybean Export Council, said China remains a vital market for U.S. soybeans, while other American agricultural sectors are also keen to expand their presence in the Chinese market. Salinas said the council took part in the China International Import Expo, which concluded in Shanghai earlier this month, as part of a broader U.S. agricultural delegation. The delegation showcased not only soybeans but also a range of other American agricultural products, including grains and almonds. Scott St John, chairman of ANZ Bank New Zealand, said he had taken the opportunity to spend more time in Shenzhen and the wider region in south China's Guangdong province, visiting companies and building connections with Chinese businesses that could complement their own operations back home. The summit has sent a powerful message to the world: it is open to the world, welcomes businesses to come and explore opportunities in China, and is equally keen to reach out, promoting open and free trade for shared prosperity, he said. From New Zealand's perspective as a pro-trade nation in the Asia-Pacific, he said, "We see China as a partner that is of a similar mind." OPPOSING PROTECTIONISM At the summit, participants voiced a common concern: rising protectionism and trade barriers will only make it harder to address global challenges. Against a backdrop of heightened uncertainty, economic disruptions and supply chain pressures, they stressed the need to keep markets open and strengthen economic ties. Low Kian Chuan, chairman of Malaysia-China Business Council, pointed out that with unilateralism and protectionism on the rise, we are seeing more tariffs as well as non-tariff barriers. "All these barriers add to our costs. That is why we advocate openness," he said. Martha Delgado, president of global advisory and advocacy firm APCO for Mexico and Latin America, said that at a time of mounting disputes over tariffs, trade restrictions and tighter borders, maintaining an open-minded approach was more important than ever. APEC economies should continue to strengthen their own economic capabilities while deepening regional integration, helping the Asia-Pacific consolidate its position as a major global economic powerhouse, Delgado said. Vicente Roqueni, executive president of the China Chamber of Commerce and Technology Mexico, said at a time when the world is facing so many challenges, China's efforts to promote cooperation and help countries achieve common development are particularly important. By lowering trade barriers, countries can expand commerce, promote shared prosperity and deepen collaboration, working toward a vision of a community where growth and opportunities are shared by all, he said. ■

item.title: Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen, calling for continued efforts to jointly steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations in the right direction toward the future. Trump is in the southern Chinese city for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi said that China-U.S. relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, bringing tangible benefits to people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world. Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new vision to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and given it new substance grounded in respect, fairness and reciprocity. The new vision has been welcomed by the people of both China and the United States, as well as the international community, he added. Xi stressed that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented and pioneering endeavor, adding that the key to sustaining the current positive momentum lies in taking concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. Xi called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns, and work toward mutual benefit. The cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity. China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence (AI) and ensure that AI always remains under human control, he said. On the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-U.S. relations, Xi said. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of U.S.-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger. Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted. He called on both sides to maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence. The United States does not support "Taiwan independence," Trump said. He congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping poses for a group photo with leaders and representatives from other economies before the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. Xi chaired the meeting and delivered important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" on Thursday. item.title: Xi urges actively addressing population aging
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
BEIJING, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged further efforts to implement the national strategy of actively addressing population aging and to ensure happier and more fulfilling lives for elderly people. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on work related to aging. Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, China has made fresh progress in responding to population aging, with both elderly care services and the elderly care industry developing at a rapid pace, Xi said. Xi emphasized the importance of coordinating efforts among the government, market, society and families and further strengthening social security, elderly care services, health services, and social participation for older people. He also stressed the need to boost the silver economy and build an age-friendly society. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national meeting on aging held from Wednesday to Thursday in Beijing. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, attended and delivered a speech at the meeting. Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, attends a national meeting on aging and delivers a speech in Beijing, capital of China. The national meeting on aging was held from Wednesday to Thursday in Beijing. An instruction of Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, was conveyed at the meeting. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) Li stressed the need to take a balanced perspective on the far-reaching implications of an aging population, be fully aware of China's unique advantages in addressing this demographic shift, and act with a stronger sense of responsibility and greater proactivity to advance work in this area. With the goal of enhancing the wellbeing of elderly people, efforts should be made to meet their needs for a better life and deliver on key tasks concerning elderly people, Li said. China has the world's largest elderly population. By the end of 2025, China had 323.38 million people aged 60 and above, or 23 percent of the population. The figure is projected to exceed 400 million by around 2035. ■

item.title: Full text
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, and delivered important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle." The following is the full text of the remarks: Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle Remarks by H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China At the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting Shenzhen, November 19, 2026 Dear Colleagues, I am delighted to welcome you to the beautiful city of Shenzhen to discuss the future of Asia-Pacific cooperation. The launch of APEC more than 30 years ago started a remarkable journey toward building an Asia-Pacific community. Over three decades and more, our region has witnessed progress with each passing day, and created the Asia-Pacific miracle of rapid economic growth. Today, momentous changes not seen in a century are accelerating across the globe. Innovation is burgeoning across sciences, technologies and industries. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, we must adapt to the new realities, take new strides, and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation. Together, we must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. -- Building an Asia-Pacific community requires solidarity and mutual assistance. The vast Pacific Ocean, which carries thousands of ships and nurtures all life, has shaped the all-embracing character of the Asia-Pacific region -- one defined by inclusiveness and harmonious coexistence. Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other. We must expand our shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily build a shared sense of community. -- Building an Asia-Pacific community requires openness and integration. Open cooperation is a sure path to the development and revitalization of the Asia-Pacific. We should uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration and develop a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated, rather than exclusive or fragmented. We should champion free and open trade and investment, remove impediments to the flow of factors, ensure the smooth circulation of economic lifeblood, and open up more space for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific. -- Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation. Innovation is the primary driving force of development. It is vital to encourage scientific and technological exchanges and cooperation, facilitate the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and foster an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. We need to carry forward our enterprising spirit, enhance APEC's role as an incubator to encourage innovation in institutions and ideas as well as structural reform, and further unleash the economic dynamism and potential of our region. -- Building an Asia-Pacific community requires inclusive development. Each with different development needs, Asia-Pacific economies are known for our diversity. We should advance cooperation where conditions allow, make sure development benefits everyone, deliver for the people, accommodate the comfort level of all parties, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. Dear Colleagues, China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation. We would like to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community. First, we should strengthen the pillar of economy and trade. The Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) is a shared vision of APEC members. It is important to make steady progress in realizing this vision and setting a higher standard for openness. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment. It is also important to enhance policy dialogue on the FTAAP, and carry out experience sharing and technical cooperation, to help the parties build capacity for participating in high-standard economic and trade arrangements. Second, we should upgrade the pillar of connectivity. Connectivity is a nexus of regional economic integration. In 2014, we jointly developed the APEC Connectivity Blueprint. Today, there are new opportunities for regional connectivity. We should strengthen physical connectivity by improving the infrastructure network, and developing smart customs and smart transportation. We should deepen institutional connectivity by harmonizing policies and regulations, deepening cooperation on cross-border payment, and keeping industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. We should also enhance people-to-people connectivity by facilitating travel for business, tourism and other purposes, and promoting cultural exchanges for better mutual understanding and closer ties among our peoples. Third, we should foster the pillar of innovation. The digital economy and artificial intelligence (AI) are the engines of innovation-driven growth. We should strengthen digital infrastructure development, improve data governance and collaboration in the region, and achieve efficient, convenient and secure cross-border data flow. We should build an open ecosystem for innovation, encourage the broad application of AI, and promote the innovation-driven transformation and upgrading of industries. Fourth, we should enhance the pillar of development. To respond to constantly emerging global challenges, we should strengthen capacity building, promote regional cooperation on energy and food security, and deepen anti-corruption governance across borders. We should coordinate the development of resources, the environment and population, scale up the rational utilization and protection of natural resources, and expand green and low-carbon cooperation to achieve sustainable economic growth. We should support livelihood improvements and invest in the people, launch healthy aging programs, facilitate employment and the development of vocational skills, and support women's economic empowerment and young talent exchanges to tap into the full potential of talent across the Asia-Pacific. China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation. I hereby announce that China will provide 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC's practical cooperation. We will establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support. In line with the needs of Asia-Pacific cooperation, we will set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of SMEs, to contribute to innovation-driven and green growth in the Asia-Pacific. Dear Colleagues, Shenzhen is known as the City of the Roc (named after a legendary bird of great size and strength). I hope that with our joint efforts, Asia-Pacific cooperation will spread its wings like the roc, and fly high and far to a bright future. Thank you. ■

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. ■ (Video reporters: Liu Yutian, Dong Bohan, Wei Ying, Wang Ruiping and Huo Siying; video editors: Liu Yutian, Hui Peipei, Mu Xuyao, Zhang Zhihuan and Zheng Xin)
